question: How do I appeal my real estate assessment?

nuggets.text: The board of equalization hears assessment complaints.
nuggets.quote: The board shall hear and give consideration to such complaints and shall adjust and equalize such assessments and shall, moreover, be charged with the especial duty of increasing as well as decreasing assessments, whether specific complaint be laid or not, if in its judgment, the same be necessary to equalize and

nuggets.text: A taxpayer may apply to the circuit court to correct an erroneous assessment.
nuggets.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made.

nuggets.text: The court application is due within three years of the last day of the tax year.
nuggets.quote: (a) within three years from the last day of the tax year for which any such assessment is made, (b) within one year from the date of the assessment, (c) within one year from the date of the Tax Commissioner's final determination under subdivision A 6 of § 58.1-3703.1 or subsection D of § 58.1-3983.1 , or (d) within

nuggets.text: In Charlottesville the appeal starts with the City Assessor.
The application is due by the date on the notice (March 4, 2026 for the 2026 assessment).
